newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles agency calls for subway delays - paper.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles agency calls for subway delays - paper.

text.p: A plan unveiled by the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority to deal with its funding shortfall would delay completion of subway projects, according to a published report Wednesday.

Under the plan, commuters would have to wait two years longer than expected to take a subway to the Eastside and seven years longer to take it to Mid-City, the Los Angeles Times reported. The authority is now projecting that the subway will not be completed to the Eastside until 2004 and to Mid-City until 2009, according to the report.
In recent weeks, the Los Angeles transportation authority has come under increasing fire from federal officials over planning, funding and management changes.

In a January 6 letter to the authority, Federal Transit Administrator Gordon Linton expressed concerns about the agency's ability to manage its projects in the face of cost overruns and a projected $1 billion hole in the county's long-range transportation plan, the Times reported.
